headline.text: The FDA label says alcohol may add to zuranolone's CNS depression and psychomotor impairment.

reported.text: The crossover trial found increased cognitive effects without increased duration and reported no pharmacokinetic interactions.

mechanism.text: The FDA label attributes increased impairment to additive pharmacological effects.

claims.text: The FDA label says alcohol with zuranolone may increase psychomotor impairment or CNS depression through additive pharmacological effects.
claims.quote: Due to additive pharmacological effects, the concomitant use of CNS depressant drugs, including alcohol, may increase impairment of psychomotor performance or CNS depressant effects.
claims.judgeRationale: The interaction table states alcohol, through additive pharmacological effects, may increase psychomotor impairment or CNS depressant effects.

claims.text: A randomized crossover trial reported greater cognitive effects with zuranolone and ethanol than with single-agent administration, without longer duration.
claims.quote: Coadministration with alprazolam/ethanol increased the magnitude, but not the duration, of effects compared with single-agent administration.
claims.judgeRationale: The phase 1 randomized crossover abstract states coadministration with alprazolam/ethanol increased the magnitude but not the duration of cognitive effects versus single agents, and separately reports worsened decline with ethanol.

claims.text: The zuranolone crossover trial, which evaluated ethanol and alprazolam combinations, reported no pharmacokinetic interactions.
claims.judgeRationale: The same trial abstract states no pharmacokinetic interactions were observed.

sources.title: Cognitive effects, pharmacokinetics, and safety of zuranolone administered alone or with alprazolam or ethanol in healthy adults in a phase 1 trial.
